name: riichiprac 2.5D shell baker
status: Phase 1c refinement: per-slot front/back wall perspectives. The camera, base scale, nine-shell base catalogue, 2-tile stack, face-up dora shells, diffuse contact shadow and side-wall lateral perspective are unchanged. The front (bottom) and back (top) walls gain a fan of per-slot shells so the tile straight in front of the human is straight on and the outer slots reveal their side, from the human's eye. Faces, atlas, layout and renderer are still later phases.

stack.note: A wall column is a stack of two tiles built from the same single shell perspective (Tenhou-style: the perspective does not change down the column even though it physically would). The bottom tier is a face-down wall shell; the top tier is the same shell offset by the published stackStepPx, or the face-up dora shell for a revealed indicator. The stack step is the projected thickness (straight up), not the face grid step.

lighting.convention: World axes: +X is screen right, -Y is toward the viewer/human edge, +Z is up off the felt. The key is one virtual light locked to screen-space top-left-front: its reference vector is authored for a front-elevation camera (azimuth 0 fronts -Y, 90 is +X, 180 is +Y, 270 is -X; elevation is above horizontal) and is then re-expressed in each shell camera's own basis (screen right, screen up, toward viewer) every time the camera moves. Highlights therefore land on the top/left of the sprite and shadows on the bottom/right in every projection, including the top-down and oblique ones.
lighting.status: Phase 1 bake. The screen-space remap is what makes one key work for six different cameras.

baseScale.note: Phase 1b decision: the Phase 1 @2x output is the new @1x base. The long axis of the projected tile body is now 104 CSS px at @1x (was 52) and 208 px at @2x, so the board coordinate space doubles in both axes and every consumer must read the new shells.json. Render real pixels at the new resolution; never upscale the Phase 1 textures. The 3-4 px right/bottom shadow and 1-2 px top/left AO contract is unchanged in pixels at the new @1x.

bake.note: One render of the tile on transparent film plus one render of the Cycles shadow catcher under it, per scale. The catcher alpha gives the physical shadow shape; it is clamped to the declared padding (3-4 px right/bottom) and normalised so the overhang peaks at shadow.peakAlpha. The top/left ambient-occlusion fringe is analytic and bounded by the 1-2 px padding.

shadowContract.note: Phase 1b review: the Phase 1/1b contact shadow was too tight. The drop shadow is now deliberately diffuse and subtle: 10-16 px right/bottom at the new @1x (was 3-4), peak alpha 0.12 (was 0.33), an 8 px @1x blur and a gentle 16 px falloff. The top/left AO fringe stays 1-2 px and drops to peak 0.20. The check enforces these ranges.

audition.status: Proposals only: front/back wall fan-strength calibration. The committed fan is the physical eye distance (front 40.8, back 54.8 units). These candidates keep the outer slot's lateral offset (-6 units) and move the eye closer/further, so the amount of side reveal at the wall end can be picked. Written under build/ (gitignored); the committed shells are never touched.
audition.deliverable: Three eye distances for the outer slot of the front and back walls, each rendered as a six-tile packed row plus an isolated tile (the isolated tile shows the full side reveal), with the camera, body, face ratio and bytes printed. Compare against the REF committed slot at the physical distance.
audition.references: Each sheet shows the committed outer slot as REF (front slot 16 at 8.37 deg, back slot 16 at 6.25 deg). The lateral offset is fixed at -6 units; only the eye distance changes, so the candidate is a pure fan-strength change. The per-slot shells interpolate between the centre (0 deg) and that outer value.

faceVariants.status: Plan only for Phase 2 (updated 2026-11-14 after the front/back wall fan). Not implemented, not baked. The atlas is keyed by (shellType, faceVariant, tileFace), so a shell can host more than one pre-rasterised decal treatment.
faceVariants.note: A variant id names the decal's perspective slot, not a camera angle. The face-up dora shells are the top tier of a wall stack, so their decals are their own perspective slots even where the projection matches a pond shell. Face-down wall shells are bare and contribute no atlas entries. The per-slot front/back dora shells are 34 further perspective slots (slotDora).

slotDora.note: The 17 front + 17 back face-up slot shells are their own atlas keys: each slot is a different perspective, so the dora blank cannot reuse one decal. That is 34 face-up dora shells x 37 faces = 1,258 sprites in addition to the hand/pond/sideway variants; Phase 2 must measure the packed atlas against the committed-asset budget before building it.

budgets.note: The per-slot front/back wall fan multiplies the wall shells (17 slots x 2 walls x face-down/face-up). The committed shell budget rises from 2 MiB to 4 MiB and the manifest budget from 64 KiB to 512 KiB; a board only loads the slots it draws, and the total committed asset budget is still 8 MiB with an initial hand + board load under 4 MiB.

wallSlots.note: The front/back walls are a fan of per-slot perspectives, not one shell. The tile directly in front of the human (slot 8 of 17) is straight on. Every other slot is seen from the human's eye, so the far-right tile shows its left side and the far-left tile shows its right side. The camera is the same off-axis perspective as the side walls; only its lateral offset and distance change. front = the bottom wall nearest the human; back = the top wall across the table. A slot's lateral offset is -(index - centreIndex) * stepUnits, i.e. the camera sits at the human's x on the centre line. The face-down and face-up dora shells share the slot's geometry; the back dora's glyph is rotated 180 so it reads for the far player.

front.note: The bottom wall, 40.8 units from the viewer's eye (eye at y -47.8, wall centre at y -7.0 on the 28 mm tile scale). The outer slot sees its tile at 8.4 deg, so the inner long side is visible.

back.note: The top wall, 54.8 units from the viewer's eye (eye at y -47.8, wall centre at y +7.0). The same fan is weaker: the outer slot sees its tile at 6.3 deg.
